declaration.preface:
This Sustainable Procurement Policy sets out the binding commitments, requirements and processes of Prestige Promotion Verkaufsförderung & Werbeservice GmbH ("Prestige Promotion") with respect to the responsible and sustainable selection, qualification, management and development of its suppliers and business partners.

As a specialist in pharmaceutical co-packaging, repackaging, contract packaging and storage of pharmaceuticals and medical devices, Prestige Promotion recognises that its supply chain has a material impact on environmental, social and ethical outcomes. This policy gives concrete expression to the company's Sustainability Code of Conduct for Suppliers & Customers and translates those commitments into a systematic procurement management framework covering two primary dimensions: Supplier Environmental Practices and Supplier Social Practices.

This policy complements and is read together with the company's QHSE Environmental Policy (POL-ENV-001), QHSE Ethics Policy (POL-ETH-001), and Labour and Human Rights Policy (POL-LHR-001).
declaration.declaration:
Integrating environmental and social sustainability criteria as mandatory evaluation factors in all supplier selection and qualification processes, alongside quality, price and delivery performance

Communicating the Sustainability Code of Conduct for Suppliers & Customers to all direct suppliers and requiring their written acknowledgement as a condition of business

Conducting systematic risk assessments of the supply chain with regard to environmental and human rights risks, in compliance with the LkSG and aligned with international due diligence frameworks

Allocating the resources — personnel, tools, and training — necessary to implement and continuously improve the sustainable procurement programme

Providing transparent communication of sustainability requirements to all suppliers and providing access to guidance, tools and support to facilitate compliance

Reviewing and updating this policy at least annually, incorporating changes in law (LkSG, EU Taxonomy), and operational experience

Applying appropriate corrective measures — up to and including termination of the business relationship — in the event of material supplier non-compliance with sustainability requirements
declaration.scope:
All procurement and purchasing activities of Prestige Promotion, including raw materials, packaging components, indirect supplies, services and logistics

All employees involved in supplier selection, evaluation, contracting or management — in particular the Purchasing / Procurement function, Quality Assurance, and Management

All direct and indirect suppliers, subcontractors, service providers and business partners of Prestige Promotion, to the extent contractually agreed

The entire supply chain relevant to Prestige Promotion's operations, including sub-tier suppliers where material sustainability risks are identified

Supplier Environmental Practices: Prestige Promotion is committed to working exclusively with suppliers that demonstrate responsible management of their environmental impacts. We expect all suppliers to comply with applicable environmental laws as a minimum baseline and to work towards continuous improvement of their environmental performance in alignment with the requirements set out in our Sustainability Code of Conduct. Environmental performance is a material criterion in supplier selection, evaluation and continued business.
The environmental requirements below apply to all direct suppliers. These requirements are aligned with the company's own ISO 14001-certified environmental management system.

Identify and monitor their greenhouse gas emissions across Scope 1 (direct), Scope 2 (purchased energy) and, where material, Scope 3 (value chain) emission sources in accordance with the GHG Protocol or an equivalent recognised methodology
Set and work towards quantitative targets for the reduction of GHG emissions; key suppliers are expected to disclose their emission reduction targets and progress annually
Monitor, document and optimise the energy efficiency of their production, logistics and facility operations, and actively seek economically viable solutions for reducing energy consumption
Prefer renewable energy sources for their electricity and heat demand where technically and economically feasible, and disclose the renewable energy share in their energy mix
Apply a systematic approach to identify, quantify, reduce and responsibly dispose of or recycle all solid waste streams — prioritising prevention and reduction at source over disposal

Manage hazardous waste in compliance with applicable regulations, including the Basel Convention (prohibition on export of hazardous waste) and national waste legislation; hazardous waste must be properly characterised, segregated, labelled, stored and handed to licensed disposal contractors

Identify and manage all chemicals and hazardous substances safely during handling, transportation, storage, use, recycling and disposal; Mercury must comply with the Minamata Convention; persistent organic pollutants must comply with the Stockholm Convention
Provide data on total waste generated, recycling rate and hazardous waste volume upon request as part of the annual sustainability review
Actively pursue circular economy principles — including the use of recycled materials, design for recyclability, and reduction of single-use materials
Monitor and document water consumption from all sources (municipal supply, groundwater, surface water); track and report water withdrawal and discharge volumes
Implement measures to reduce water consumption and prevent wastewater generation at source

Characterise, monitor and treat all industrial and process wastewater before discharge or disposal in compliance with applicable regulatory standards; no untreated wastewater may be discharged into the environment
Protect water quality and availability for local communities — suppliers must not deprive persons of access to clean drinking water or sanitary facilities through their operations
Continuously reduce the use and consumption of raw materials, energy, water and other natural resources through process optimisation, material substitution, and waste minimisation
Monitor and document consumption of key raw materials and natural resources, and set reduction targets where material consumption is significant
Supplier Social Practices: Prestige Promotion is committed to working exclusively with suppliers that respect human rights, provide fair and safe working conditions, and uphold the dignity of all people in their operations and supply chains. These requirements reflect the company's obligations under the German Supply Chain Due Diligence Act (LkSG), the UN Guiding Principles on Business and Human Rights, and the ILO Core Conventions, and give concrete expression to the social responsibility requirements of the Prestige Promotion Sustainability Code of Conduct.

Non-compliance with the social requirements below is considered a material supplier non-conformity and may result in escalation, enhanced corrective action requirements, or termination of the business relationship.
No supplier may use child labour at any stage of production, processing, assembly or service delivery; this prohibition applies without exception, regardless of local custom or practice

The minimum employment age must be the age at which compulsory schooling ends under the law of the place of employment and in any case not below 18 years of age, in accordance with ILO Convention No. 138; in countries where the minimum age for hazardous work is higher, that higher age applies
Suppliers must verify the age of all workers — including temporary, seasonal and agency workers — before employment commences, and must document the verification process

All work must be voluntary — employees must be free to leave their employment with reasonable notice and must not be subject to debt bondage, indentured labour, or any form of coercion that restricts their freedom to terminate employment
Suppliers must not retain workers' identity documents or personal property; no recruitment fees or deposits may be charged to workers that create a binding financial dependency
No supplier may use psychological coercion, physical threats, sexual harassment or humiliation, or any other form of improper treatment that undermines the dignity or autonomy of workers

Suppliers must implement and maintain an occupational health and safety management system covering identification and prevention of workplace hazards, provision of appropriate PPE, emergency preparedness, and incident reporting

Appropriate precautionary measures must be taken against accidents and health hazards — including physical, chemical, biological, ergonomic and psychosocial hazards; excessive physical or mental fatigue must be prevented
All workers must have access to adequate drinking water and clean sanitary facilities at all times; workplace facilities must meet applicable health and hygiene standards
Employees must be regularly trained on health and safety standards, risks relevant to their work, and safe working procedures; training records must be maintained
Suppliers must report any work-related fatalities, serious injuries or significant occupational health incidents to Prestige Promotion without delay

Any form of discrimination in employment — including recruitment, remuneration, training, promotion, and termination — on the grounds of gender, nationality, ethnic origin, skin colour, disability, health status, pregnancy, age, religion, political conviction, sexual identity or any other protected characteristic is prohibited
The personal dignity, privacy and personal rights of every worker must be respected; psychological, physical or sexual harassment or humiliation of any kind is prohibited
Suppliers must implement a documented procedure for reporting and handling complaints of discrimination or harassment, ensuring workers can raise concerns without fear of retaliation

Integration with QMS; supplier audit coordination; document control; LkSG documentation and annual report

policy.monitoring:
The following overarching quantitative targets govern the sustainable procurement programme as a whole. They provide a consolidated, programme-level view of ambition across all supplier sustainability dimensions and are monitored annually by the Purchasing function and Quality Management Officer, reviewed in the management review.

Base year: 2025.
policy.reviewMechanism:
Review for currency and compliance with changes in law (LkSG, EU Taxonomy, CSRD

Annual update of programme-level targets against actual performance; new targets set for following year

Semi-annual review of quantitative environmental and social targets by Purchasing / QMO

Integration of supplier sustainability performance data into annual QM management review (QMH Chapter 5.7)

Annual supply chain risk report documenting due diligence activities, findings and remediation measures

In the event of supplier incidents, new legislation, or significant supply chain changes
